questions.question: Which House of the Indian Parliament is more powerful?

options.text: Both Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lok Sabha**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Lok Sabha** is more powerful than the Rajya Sabha in the Indian Parliament.
 
• While both houses participate in the legislative process, the Lok Sabha has greater authority in financial matters.
 
• Money bills can only be introduced in the Lok Sabha, and the Rajya Sabha can only make recommendations which the Lok Sabha may accept or reject.
 
• The Lok Sabha can also override the Rajya Sabha in case of a disagreement on ordinary bills through a joint sitting.
 
• Additionally, the Council of Ministers is responsible to the Lok Sabha, and it can pass a vote of no confidence to remove the government.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Lok Sabha** is the lower house of India's bicameral Parliament and is directly elected by the people.
 
• The **Rajya Sabha** is the upper house, with members elected by the elected members of State Legislative Assemblies, and by the members of the Electoral college for Union Territories.
 
• The maximum strength of the Lok Sabha is 552 members, whereas the Rajya Sabha has a maximum of 250 members.
 
• The term of the Lok Sabha is five years unless dissolved earlier, while the Rajya Sabha is a permanent body with one-third of its members retiring every two years.

questions.question: Vallabh Bhai Patel was first associated with which movement of Mahatma Gandhi?
questions.solution:
```html

**The correct answer is - __Kheda Satyagraha__**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__ **

__
 
• **Kheda Satyagraha__**

 __
 
• **Vallabh Bhai Patel__** was first associated with Mahatma Gandhi through the **__Kheda Satyagraha__**, which occurred in 1918.
 
• The **__Kheda Satyagraha__** was a significant movement aimed at supporting farmers in the Kheda district of Gujarat, who were unable to pay taxes due to famine and crop failure.
 
• Patel played a pivotal role in organizing and mobilizing farmers, establishing his leadership and close association with Gandhi.
 
• The movement was based on the principles of **__nonviolent resistance__**, marking a major milestone in India's struggle for independence.
 
 

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] __Additional Information__ **

__
 
• **Champaran Satyagraha__**

 __
 
• This was Mahatma Gandhi's first major Satyagraha in India (1917), but Vallabh Bhai Patel was not directly associated with this movement.
 
• The Champaran Satyagraha aimed to address the exploitation of indigo farmers in Bihar.
 
 
 
• **Non-Cooperation Movement__**
 __
 
• Launched by Gandhi in 1920, this movement aimed at boycotting British goods and institutions.
 
• Patel played an important role in this movement later, but it was not his first association with Gandhi.
 
 
 
• **Dandi March__**
 
 
• The Dandi March (1930) was a part of the Civil Disobedience Movement led by Gandhi to protest against the salt tax.
 
• Though Patel was an active participant, this was much later in his political career.
 
 

``

questions.question: Identify the classical dance native to Uttar Pradesh among these.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kathak**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Kathak** is one of the eight classical dances of India and is native to Uttar Pradesh.
 
• It derives its name from the Sanskrit word “Katha,” meaning story, and is known for its storytelling through intricate footwork and gestures.
 
• Kathak is characterized by rhythmic footwork, spins, and expressive gestures combined with graceful movements.
 
• It evolved during ancient times and gained prominence during the Mughal era, blending Persian and Hindu traditions.
 
• Prominent gharanas (schools) of Kathak include the Lucknow, Jaipur, and Banaras gharanas, each with distinct features and styles.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Odissi:**

 
 
• Odissi is a classical dance form originating from Odisha, India.
 
• It is known for its lyrical movements and is inspired by temple sculptures and poses.
 
• Odissi is traditionally performed as a devotional offering to Lord Jagannath.
 
• It emphasizes "Tribhangi" (three bends of the body) and "Chauka" (square stance).
 
 
 
• **Therukkootthu:**
 
 
• Therukkootthu is a folk dance-drama native to Tamil Nadu, not a classical dance form.
 
• It is performed in open spaces to narrate stories from epics like Mahabharata and Ramayana.
 
• This art form is characterized by vibrant costumes, makeup, and theatrical performances.
 
• Therukkootthu is primarily a rural tradition and not recognized as a classical dance.
 
 
 
• **Mohiniattam:**
 
 
• Mohiniattam is a classical dance form native to Kerala.
 
• It is performed by women and is characterized by gentle and graceful movements.
 
• The dance is closely associated with the mythological enchantress Mohini, an avatar of Lord Vishnu.
 
• Mohiniattam uses elements of Bharatanatyam and Kathakali, focusing on Lasya (feminine grace).

questions.question: The hills of the northeast are called _____.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Purvanchal__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/fed23cf83dbb708fc244a9fb2551a628789543fa05ad81abd91932195698c9cd.png] 

__
 
• Hills including Mishmi, **Naga, Manipur, Tripura, Mizo, Patkai** that run through the **north-east region** are known as **Purvanchal Hills**.
 
• It lies **south of the Brahmaputra valley**.
 
• It covers an area of about **94,800 km².**
 
• It covers **Nagaland, Manipur, Tripura, and Mizoram Hills**, and Chachar Districts along with a fifth of **Haflong tahsil of** **Assam **State and District of Tripa and part of **Lohit in Arunachal Pradesh**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bharamputra River enters first** in **Namchafarua mountain** in **Arunachal Pradesh**.
 
• **Majuli Island in Assam is the world's largest river island.**
 
• **Tributaries** of **Bharamputra **are - **Manas, Tista**, **Jamuna**, **Dihand, Dibang**, Kemeng, etc.
 
• **Cities alongside the river Bharamputra** are - **Guwahati, Dibrugarh**.

questions.question: Which is the project to clean the river Ganga started by the Government of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Namami Gange.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Namami Gange** is the project to clean the river Ganga launched by the Government of India.
 
• The project integrates the efforts to clean and protect the Ganga River in a comprehensive manner.
 
 
• It was approved as a ‘Flagship Programme’ by the Union Government in **June 2014.**
 
• The main objectives of the Namami Gange project are:
 
 
• Effective abatement of pollution.
 
• Conservation and rejuvenation of National River Ganga.
 
 
 
• It is being implemented by the **National Mission for Clean Ganga (NMCG)**, and its State Program Management Groups.
 
• The Ganga serves as one of India's holiest rivers whose cultural and spiritual significance transcends the boundaries of the basin.
 
• The **Centre funds 100%** of the Namami Gange project.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Polavaram Project **is an under-construction multi-purpose irrigation project in Andhra Pradesh.
 
• The** Kalpasar Project** is a water resources project by way of building an Over Sea dam across the Gulf of Khambhat.
 
 
• It is also called the Gulf of Khambhat Development Project.
 
 
 
• **Ganga Manthan** was a national conference conducted to discuss issues and possible solutions for cleaning the river.

questions.question: Which scheme focuses specifically on supporting organic farming?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**PKVY**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **PKVY (Paramparagat Krishi Vikas Yojana)** focuses specifically on supporting **organic farming** practices in India. It was launched in **2015** to promote sustainable agriculture and reduce the dependency on chemical fertilizers and pesticides.
 
• Under PKVY, clusters of farmers are encouraged to take up organic farming. Each cluster should consist of **50 or more farmers** with a total area of at least **50 acres**.
 
• The scheme provides financial assistance of up to **₹50,000 per hectare** for a period of three years to support organic farming activities. This includes assistance for **organic certification, training, and the adoption of organic practices**.
 
• **PKVY** aims to promote **traditional agricultural practices**, improve soil fertility, and ensure the production of healthy and chemical-free crops. Farmers are encouraged to use natural inputs like compost, green manure, and bio-pesticides.
 
• The scheme also supports the formation of **Farmer Producer Organizations (FPOs)** to market organic produce and provide better price realization for farmers.
 
• **PKVY** is implemented in coordination with **State Governments** and emphasizes the creation of market linkages for organically produced crops. Farmers are trained and provided with necessary resources for organic farming.
 
• The scheme is part of the broader **National Mission for Sustainable Agriculture (NMSA)**, which aims to reduce the environmental impact of agriculture and promote eco-friendly farming practices.
 
• **Hence, the correct answer is PKVY.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Other Schemes Mentioned:**

 
 
• **PM-KMY (Pradhan Mantri Kisan Maan-Dhan Yojana):** This scheme provides **pension benefits** to small and marginal farmers upon attaining the age of 60 years. It is not related to organic farming.
 
• **Soil Health Card Scheme:** Launched in **2015**, this scheme aims to provide farmers with information about the **nutrient status of their soil** and recommendations for improving soil health. While it is beneficial for agriculture, it does not specifically focus on organic farming.
 
• **ATMA (Agricultural Technology Management Agency):** This scheme is part of the **National Mission on Agricultural Extension and Technology** and aims to strengthen agricultural extension services. It focuses on capacity building and technology dissemination but does not exclusively address organic farming.
 
 
 
• **Objectives of PKVY:**
 
 
• Promote the use of **indigenous practices** in agriculture.
 
• Enhance the **income of farmers** through premium pricing of organic produce.
 
• Reduce the adverse effects of **chemical-based farming** on soil, water, and human health.
 
• Encourage the adoption of **natural and eco-friendly farming methods**.
 
 
 
• **Implementation of PKVY:**
 
 
• Farmers are organized into clusters and provided with training and resources for organic farming.
 
• Emphasis is placed on **organic certification** to ensure the authenticity of produce.
 
• Support is provided for setting up **vermicompost units, biogas units, and other organic farming infrastructure**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Organic Farming in India:**

 
 
• Organic farming involves the use of natural inputs like **organic compost, bio-fertilizers, and bio-pesticides**.
 
• India ranks among the top countries in terms of the number of farmers practicing organic farming, with a significant focus on states like **Sikkim, Uttarakhand, and Madhya Pradesh**.
 
• Organic farming not only improves soil health but also contributes to **environmental sustainability**.
 
 
 
• **Global Trends:**
 
 
• The global market for organic food is growing rapidly, driven by increasing awareness of the **health and environmental benefits** of organic products.
 
• Countries like **Germany, the USA, and Australia** are major markets for organic produce.

questions.question: Who has been appointed as the chairperson of the Athletics Federation of India's (AFI) Athletes Commission?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** ​Anju Bobby George**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] __In News__**

__
 
• **Anju Bobby George** appointed as **Chairperson** of the **AFI Athletes Commission** on **Jan 8, 2025**, marking a milestone with **6 women** on the **9-member panel**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

 
• Notable women members include **Jyotirmoyee Sikdar, Krishna Poonia, M.D. Valsamma, Sudha Singh**, and **Sunita Rani**.
 
• **Neeraj Chopra**, **two-time Olympic medalist**, is the most prominent **male member** of the commission, alongside **Avinash Sable** and **Bahadur Singh Sagoo** (new AFI president).
 
• The **commission** was unveiled following **October 2024 elections**, with **five members elected** and **four nominated** after consultation with the **AFI Executive Council**.
 
• **Outgoing AFI president Adille Sumariwalla** remains **ex-officio member** and will chair a **committee for government and international liaison**, also serving on the **AFI Ethics Commission**.
 
• **Federation Cup 2025** will be held in **Kozhikode, Kerala**, from **April 21-24**, after Haryana's withdrawal due to scheduling conflicts.
